1_sample_support.question: Whether training images contain sufficient flat-lay examples
1_sample_support.findings: Out of 4,412 training images in Phase 14.0, only 39 were flat-lays (0.88%). Over 95.7% of the dataset consisted of on-body street and lifestyle photography.

2_human_body_context.question: Whether the model learned human-body context instead of garment features
2_human_body_context.findings: Because 95.7% of training images had human subjects, convolutional filters optimized for facial, arm, and leg contours rather than intrinsic garment structural elements (waistbands, hemlines, collars). When a human is absent, activations collapse to background classes.

3_background_dominance.question: Whether backgrounds dominate image embeddings
3_background_dominance.findings: On-body images feature vertical 3D perspective scenes (streets, interiors). Flat-lays have solid 2D flat surfaces (wood floors, bedsheets, studio white). The model correlates planar surface textures with fabric wraps like sarees and shawls, systematically predicting 'traditional' (saree, kurta).

4_mask_usage_during_training.question: Whether garment masks are being used during training
4_mask_usage_during_training.findings: Phase 14.0 training scripts fed raw RGB images directly to the backbone without mask conditioning or background suppression. The network never learned to isolate garment pixels from background environments.

5_aspect_ratio_divergence.question: Whether flat-lay garments have different aspect-ratio distributions
5_aspect_ratio_divergence.findings: On-body crops average an aspect ratio of 1.676 (tall portrait), whereas flat-lays average 1.13 (square/landscape, min 0.45, max 1.52). This 2.1x aspect-ratio disparity creates significant out-of-distribution feature shifts.

6_sleeve_articulation.question: Whether sleeves and garment components are interpreted incorrectly
6_sleeve_articulation.findings: Laid-flat garments feature splayed or folded sleeves perpendicular to the body axis. On-body garments feature sleeves draped vertically alongside the torso. Horizontal sleeves break the vertical contour prior learned by MobileNetV3.

7_taxonomy_consistency.question: Whether the dataset taxonomy is consistent across image types
7_taxonomy_consistency.findings: The 10-domain and 55-subcategory taxonomy is ontology-consistent across modalities, but the tree masking prior was unconditional on image type, preventing the network from applying flat-lay specific silhouette hypotheses.

8_resizing_distortion.question: Whether flat-lay images are being resized or cropped incorrectly
8_resizing_distortion.findings: Standard transforms.Resize((224, 224)) non-isotropically squashed wide landscape flat-lays into squares. For folded chinos (AR 1.52), squashing compressed the leg folds into a horizontal block, causing the network to predict 'footwear -> sneakers' with 68.9% confidence.

9_gradient_class_imbalance.question: Whether class imbalance causes flat-lay-specific failure
9_gradient_class_imbalance.findings: In random mini-batch sampling (batch size 64), the average flat-lay occurrence was 0.56 samples per batch. Over 55% of batches contained zero flat-lays, causing flat-lay gradients to be completely erased by on-body gradients.

10_backbone_feature_discrimination.question: Whether the current backbone can distinguish isolated garments from background clutter
10_backbone_feature_discrimination.findings: MobileNetV3-Small possesses sufficient parameter capacity (1.08M parameters) to recognize isolated garments, but requires domain-aware supervision, aspect-ratio letterboxing, and background suppression to prevent body-context shortcutting.
